props.title: Green Room
props.initialSlug: Survive the night or die trying.

sections.content: **Green Room** (2016) stands as one of the most intense siege thrillers of the 2010s. Director Jeremy Saulnier crafts a brutal, claustrophobic nightmare when a punk band witnesses a murder at a neo-Nazi club. Like **Assault on Precinct 13** (1976), it traps protagonists in a hostile space, but Saulnier adds raw punk energy and unflinching violence. Patrick Stewart delivers a chilling performance as the methodical skinhead leader, while Anton Yelchin leads the desperate band members with tangible fear and determination.

sections.content: The film builds on a tradition of punk rock cinema that includes **The Decline of Western Civilization** (1981) and **Return of the Living Dead** (1985). But where those films celebrated punk's anarchic energy, **Green Room** uses the subculture as a backdrop for primal survival horror. The authenticity of the punk scenes comes from Saulnier's own experience in the DC hardcore scene, giving weight to the band's dynamics and performances.

Beyond its genre thrills, **Green Room** offers a stark look at modern American extremism, predating the increased visibility of white supremacist groups. Like **American History X** (1998) and **This Is England** (2006), it explores racist subcultures without sensationalism, showing their mundane organizational structure alongside their capacity for violence. sections.content: The film's technical elements deserve special attention. Cinematographer Sean Porter creates a sickly green palette that enhances the trapped feeling, while the sound design emphasizes every impact. The violence, though extreme, serves the story rather than exploitation. This approach aligns with other modern siege films like **Don't Breathe** (2016) and **You're Next** (2011), where brutality has consequence rather than entertainment value.
